title: structured output: add constrained-decoding backends (CFG + regex) and tokenizer-aware checks
author: Priya Khandelwal
description:
Motivation: Add first-class constrained decoding backends to the structured-output pipeline so we can express and enforce outputs as CFGs or regexes while remaining robust to tokenizer edge cases and streaming. This PR implements a pluggable ConstrainedDecoding abstraction with two initial backends (CFG-based and regex-based), tokenizer-alignment utilities, and streaming-aware incremental checkers.

Summary of changes: 1) core/api: Introduced constrained_decoding interface and engine wiring to the structured-output service so calls can pass constraint payloads (grammar or regex) in the same API envelope used for other structured-output options. 2) backends/cfg_backend: New CFG compiler that converts a simplified context-free grammar into a compact deterministic PDA representation used for token-sequence validation and incremental streaming checks. The compiler includes a small grammar sanity checker and useful error messages for invalid or ambiguous grammars. 3) backends/regex_backend: Regex backend compiles provided regexes to a NFA/DFA over Unicode codepoints and then uses tokenizer mapping heuristics to validate token sequences. Supports anchored, multi-line, and capturing-group-aware constraints where applicable. 4) tokenizer/utils: Added tokenizer alignment helpers to map character-level constraints to token boundaries and incremental heuristics to avoid rejecting valid tokenization splits (handles byte-pair edge tokens and special tokens). 5) streaming: Implemented incremental constraint validation so partial streamed tokens can be validated without blocking until eos. 6) api/openai_compat: Updated OpenAI compatibility layer to accept "constraints" field in function-calling and chat endpoints, and to translate compatibility-format constraints into internal backends. 7) tests: Added exhaustive unit tests for CFG parsing, regex tokenized matching, tokenizer edge cases (split punctuation, accent combining characters), and integration tests with the streaming path. 8) docs: Added API docs for constraints and example grammar snippets.

Design notes and tradeoffs: - We intentionally keep the grammar syntax conservative (subset of EBNF) to avoid ambiguous parses at runtime; complex grammars should be compiled offline. - Tokenizer alignment is heuristic-first: it prefers permissive matching for user-facing UX, with an option to run strict token-boundary enforcement for security-sensitive endpoints. - Regex backend works best for line-oriented constraints; for nested hierarchical output CFG gives stronger guarantees. - Performance: incremental DFA/PDA checks are optimized for common-case short constraints; in microbenchmarks we see ~10-15% added per-token CPU for strict checking on small models but remain within SLO for typical workloads.

Commits (high-level): - Add constrained_decoding interface and wiring - Implement CFG compiler and PDA runtime - Implement regex backend with token mapping - Tokenizer alignment utilities and edge-case tests - Streaming incremental checker and integration - OpenAI compat translations and examples - Add unit + integration tests - Docs and CHANGELOG entry

Files changed (high level): - core/api/structured_output.go, core/api/structured_output_test.go - backends/cfg/compiler.go, backends/cfg/runtime.go, backends/cfg/grammar_test.go - backends/regex/compiler.go, backends/regex/runtime.go, backends/regex/regex_test.go - tokenizer/align/align.go, tokenizer/align/align_test.go - streaming/constraints/incremental_checker.go - api/openai_compat/constraints_translate.go - docs/api/structured_output_constraints.md - tests/integration/streaming_constraints_test.go

CI notes: Initial CI run showed a failing unit test in tokenizer alignment for combining-accent sequences on macOS runners. Fixed by handling Unicode normalization NFKC in tokenizer alignment helper and re-ran CI. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration on x86 Linux and macOS, basic perf smoke).

Release notes: Adds constrained decoding backends (CFG and regex) for structured output with tokenizer-aware checks and streaming support. See docs for usage and example grammars.

Backward compatibility: API changes are additive. The OpenAI compatibility layer accepts an optional "constraints" field and translates it to the internal format; no existing clients are affected.

Security and sandboxing: Regex backend bounds the automaton size and rejects catastrophic regexes at compile time; CFG backend rejects left-recursive grammars and reports errors. We added a max-work budget per-request to avoid DoS from malicious constraints.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice overall design. A few asks: add benchmarks for CFG vs regex backends and prove streaming incremental check doesn't regress latency beyond SLOs.
María Velasquez: Please add more tests around emoji and complex combining characters (e.g. flag sequences). Also call out any normalization decisions in the public docs.
Ethan Zhou: Minor nit: move max-work budget to config runtime with a default and make failure reason include diagnostic token index.

Priya Khandelwal (author): Addressed comments: added perf microbenchmarks and results to docs, added emoji/combining tests, exposed MaxConstraintWork in runtime config and included diagnostic info in failures. PTAL.
Liam O'Connor: Approved after bench numbers look reasonable and tests added.
notes_on_perf: Microbenchmarks added under tests/perf show ~12% median per-token CPU increase for strict CFG checking on small models; relaxed/tokenizer-permissive mode is <3%. We documented tradeoffs in docs.
release_notes_short: Add CFG and regex constrained decoding backends for structured output; tokenizer-aware streaming validation and OpenAI compatibility updates.
